claims.text: The as-built additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy has a homogeneous FCC matrix.
The as-built alloy has a uniform elemental distribution.
Degradation during high-temperature exposure is governed by formation and retention of a protective, adherent Al/Cr-rich oxide scale.
Selective surface segregation of Cr and Ti produces or controls the proposed Al/Cr-rich oxide scale.
Under oxidizing conditions, the Al/Cr-rich scale acts as a barrier to further oxidation and degradation.
Under reducing conditions, failure to sustain a robust oxide scale causes elemental depletion and microstructural destabilization.
Surface and near-surface segregation of Cr and Ti governs oxide-scale continuity and adhesion.
Oxide-scale continuity and adhesion affect the integrity of the underlying FCC matrix.
In reducing gas, loss or inadequate development of the protective scale forms oxygen-deficient or embrittled matrix regions.
Oxygen-deficient or embrittled matrix regions accelerate degradation.
Pre-oxidation at 650°C for 2 hours in 0.2 atm O2 will induce a thin, controlled Al/Cr-rich oxide scale.
The specified pre-oxidation treatment will not affect the integrity of the FCC matrix.
In 0.2 atm O2 at 700°C, pre-oxidized samples will develop a more continuous and adherent Al/Cr-rich scale than as-built samples.
In oxidizing exposure, pre-oxidized samples will exhibit slower degradation kinetics, less oxide spallation, and slower elemental depletion than as-built samples.
Pre-oxidized samples will preserve mechanical properties better than as-built samples during oxidizing exposure.
Under reducing exposure, both pre-oxidized and as-built samples may eventually degrade.
Under reducing exposure, pre-oxidation may delay or moderate degradation relative to the as-built condition.
The as-built alloy naturally develops oxide scales during exposure.
Less-controlled scale formation in the as-built alloy causes faster spallation, elemental depletion, and degradation than in pre-oxidized samples.

No significant difference between pre-oxidized and untreated samples in scale continuity, segregation, degradation kinetics, and mechanical-property retention across both atmospheres would falsify the proposed mechanism.
